why: The repository contains the analytic CSV and the authors' analysis notebook, so the core CRP experiment is released. However, the target claim depends on TabPFN v2, whose weights/access require a manual Prior Labs license acceptance and personal token; the repo also ships notebooks rather than a runnable Python entrypoint and has no dependency lock/requirements file. The authors' logic can be kept, but the notebook path must be ported to a local script and TabPFN access supplied.
missing_artifacts: TabPFN v2 model weights / Prior Labs access token and license acceptance
requirements.txt or environment specification for exact package versions
standalone Python script entrypoint (code is only in notebooks)
local-path adaptation for Colab Drive-mount/upload cells
blockers_seen: TabPFN v2 requires a one-time interactive license acceptance and personal TABPFN_TOKEN; without that token the target TabPFN claim cannot be run
The notebook is Colab-oriented and expects /content/data/nhanes_analytic.csv after a manual upload step
No Python .py files are present; code is embedded in large notebooks
No GPU on this machine, but the paper explicitly used CPU inference, so this is not a blocker

feasibility.est_runtime_on_this_machine: About 10-20 minutes total if TabPFN access is already available: a few minutes to install, a few minutes for TabPFN v2 CPU inference on 828x18 data, and a short clean rerun. Model/package download dominates.

compute.basis: One TabPFN v2 in-context regression fit on a small 828-row, roughly 18-feature tabular dataset plus scaling and test evaluation; runtime is dominated by package/weight download and TabPFN setup, not model training.
